title: TAI public ACL isolation and deployment recovery
objective: Eliminate the two effective non-TAI relation privileges inherited by tai_runtime through PUBLIC without breaking trusted application principals, and add a deterministic wrapper-level recovery for every failed standalone TAI deployment before terminal evidence is published.
boundaries: The migration changes only table-like relations in schema public whose ACL explicitly grants a covered table privilege to PUBLIC and whose name is outside tai_*
A non-zero production correction is accepted only when exactly two distinct affected relations are present
Before PUBLIC revocation, each affected privilege is granted to every existing trusted runtime principal from the fixed set app_runtime and app_service
No tenant rows, business data, object definitions, RLS policies, ownership, application roles or secrets are changed
The migration is idempotent and returns without mutation when no affected PUBLIC relation ACL remains
Failed standalone deployment recovery is invoked only after the exact-main protected controller returns non-zero
Recovery is bounded to the exact run state root, exact Compose project, exact PostgreSQL authority and the dedicated tai_runtime principal
Recovery removes the partial TAI container, restores exact env and Compose snapshots and revokes only ACL entries whose grantee is tai_runtime
Recovery refuses role removal when memberships, active sessions, ownership or default ACL dependencies are present
DROP OWNED, REASSIGN OWNED, database object deletion, PUBLIC mutation during recovery, tenant mutation and financial authority expansion are forbidden
The original deployment exit code remains failure even after recovery; recovery only makes rollback status truthful and production state safe
Successful deployment remains responsible for exact-main TAI service materialization, live acceptance, durable evidence and rollback authority
REG.RU only and no new recurring cost
